title: CS amp, resistive load
description: Common-source stage with a physical resistor as the load. $g_m$ is fixed from the bandwidth spec (with an explicit over-design factor) and $g_m/I_D$ is the efficiency knob; the load resistor $R_{load}$ sets both the gain and the DC drop that eats output headroom. This is the classic gain-vs-headroom trade made explicit: a bigger $R_{load}$ raises the gain but drops more of the supply, so the output DC level $V_{out}$ = VDD - $I*R_{load}$ sinks toward the device's saturation floor. $V_{out}$ is an estimate used to bias the device; the headroom-consistent guardrail checks it against the actual drop, so retune $V_{out}$ (or $R_{load}$) until it is green.

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (drain + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: gbw_margin
params.note: over-design factor on gm for parasitics and PVT

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistor: higher R raises the gain but drops more of the supply (less headroom)

params.name: V_out
params.note: estimate of the output DC level, used as the device's vds; retune until the headroom-consistent guardrail is green

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance. The load knob is already inside this row and inside the gain, so the loading contract here is the arithmetic rather than a separate rule

rows.name: Av
rows.note: gm into the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance

rows.name: V_drop
rows.note: DC drop across the load resistor

rows.name: V_out_actual
rows.note: the output DC level the sized current actually produces

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: device channel thermal density plus the load resistor's 4kT/R_load current noise referred to the input by 1/gm

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents — this stage's gate capacitance and nothing else. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the branch current, which here is an OUTPUT of the sizing rather than a setting: the bandwidth spec fixes gm, and the chosen inversion divides it down to a current. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
device saturated at the DC output level the load drop leaves
computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
actual GBW into CL plus the parasitic estimate; the over-design factor should keep this green
the biasing V_out estimate should match the actual VDD - I*R_load; retune V_out or R_load if this trips
